BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Package Review Against Buyer Playbook

## Bottom line

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material economic and risk-allocation point. It describes these as "key negotiated positions," but the Buyer has not agreed them. Nothing in the package should be accepted as settled. The most serious issues are the liability cap, thresholds and basket, the time limits, the general regime applied to title and fraud, the open-ended disclosure and buyer-knowledge provisions, the Bluefen and Riverlark conditions, and the excluded AUD 420,000 bonuses.

## Departure table

| Issue | Seller position | Our playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Start 25% / AUD 6m. 20% is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft; none given | Reject. Restore 25% / AUD 6m. Do not concede 20% in correspondence |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Restore AUD 5,000 |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Reject. Restore AUD 50,000 with first-dollar recovery |
| General time limit (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval; none given) | Reject. Restore 24 months |
| Uniform limitations across claims | Caps, time limits and bars apply to "all Claims" | Separate regimes: Fundamental/Title separate, 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Reject. Restore separate regime |
| Title and capacity (fundamental) | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Title/capacity are fundamental: 100% cap, 6+ years | Reject outright |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out to the maximum enforceable extent; no waiver | Reject. Add an express fraud carve-out. Playbook says no one may waive it |
| Disclosure (1.1, 1.2, Sch 7) | Whole data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records disclosed | Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure | Reject. Limit to specific, fairly disclosed matters |
| Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | No claim for anything Buyer or advisers knew, including anything discoverable from data room or public records | Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Delete. Any knowledge qualifier must follow the playbook test |
| Bluefen (cl 3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; treat consent as satisfied on delivery of counterparty's consent | Effective consent AND evidence conditions satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer consent | Reject. Make it a condition precedent with evidence |
| Riverlark (cl 2/7) | About AUD 3.2m released "following Completion" | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases; post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking AND Amelia Frost approval | Reject. Require repayment at Completion from funds flow |
| Bonuses (funds flow; DD-005) | AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller," not in funds flow | Specific line item or Seller-funded, including triggered on-costs; not silently excluded | Reject. Add as a specific line item or Seller-funded, with on-costs |
| Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden the indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure. AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way | Reject "adequate." Broaden the indemnity |
| Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6, Sch 6) | "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction | Accept the factual uncertainty, but require log preservation, investigation and regular updates. Do not adopt "not material" |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Do not accept the characterisation. Assess each renewal's terms, whether it is terminable and whether it accrued |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain OPEN. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution | Reject. Keep these as open categories, separate from general regime |
| Title | Share register at DD-012 evidences title | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required. DD-012 is an internal source, not independent proof | Reject. Require independent evidence |

## Reasoning on the material issues

**1. Liability architecture.** The Seller has taken the 20% fallback cap and combined it with a 5x higher de minimis, a 5x higher basket and excess-only recovery. Together these shift most of the sub-AUD 250k risk onto the Buyer. The cap is also presented as settled, but the playbook only permits 20% with written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None has been given, so 20% should not be treated as on the table.

**2. Time limits and the uniform-application clause.** The 18-month period is the same fallback; 24 months applies. The "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" wording would allow the general limits to override the fundamental and fraud regimes by default. This is the "hidden general-regime override" the playbook warns against.

**3. Title and capacity.** Putting title and capacity under general caps and time limits is the most significant structural departure. Title is a fundamental warranty. Its 100% cap, six-year period and exemption from basket, de minimis and knowledge bar must remain. The "administrative simplicity" rationale is not a basis for departure.

**4. Fraud carve-out.** Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language to "all Claims of any nature." That would capture fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. The carve-out must be express and cannot be waived.

**5. Disclosure and buyer knowledge.** Paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 disclose the entire data room and public records, with 1.2 applying "without limiting any specific disclosure." Clause 8.3 then bars claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew or could have discovered. Together these create a deemed-knowledge regime the playbook rejects. The Disclosure Letter's numbering also goes from 1.2 to 1.4, so ask whether a 1.3 was removed and what it said.

**6. Bluefen.** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). Treating consent as satisfied on delivery, with only reasonable endeavours, leaves a material customer consent unresolved at Completion. The Disclosure Letter confirms no final written consent and no evidence that the conditions in 11.3 are satisfied.

**7. Riverlark.** The Disclosure Letter confirms the AUD 3.2m facility is unpaid and no discharge is included. A post-Completion release is not acceptable without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. The playbook calls for direct repayment from Completion funds, which the current funds flow does not provide.

**8. Bonuses.** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, but the funds flow omits them and does not address on-costs. The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller," but unless they are funded by the Seller in the funds flow or as a specific line item, they could become a Buyer cost without any protection.

**9. Ironquay.** Clause 7.3 of DD-004 makes transfer of SOW3 materials conditional on payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, and the Disclosure Letter confirms no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. The AUD 180,000 is not verified either way, so do not assert it is owed. But the narrow SOW3-only indemnity does not cover the broader IP risk, and "adequate" is not accepted.

**10. Incident (DD-006).** The Disclosure Letter does not characterise the event as a confirmed breach, does not confirm harm or notification, and states no loss amount. Playbook assumes none of these in either direction. The Seller's "not expected to be material" is an opinion, not a finding, and should be replaced with an investigation undertaking.

**11. Sandbar renewals.** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are described as ordinary-course, but the Disclosure Letter says it is unknown whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course. Assess before accepting the characterisation. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction should be agreed.

**12. Title evidence.** DD-012 is the share register, which the Seller relies on. It is an internal source and does not establish title independently. The Buyer needs its own verification: searches, confirmation of registration, encumbrance checks and authority evidence.

**13. Other items.** Mossvale (DD-009) and the office lease (DD-007) both involve assignment or notification provisions. The Seller says Mossvale consent is not required merely because shares are sold, and that the lease needs notice but not landlord consent. Both points need confirmation from the underlying clauses, not from the Seller's summary.

## Recommendations (priority order)

1. **Reject the Seller's characterisation** of these as negotiated positions. Put in writing that nothing is agreed, and that the Buyer's playbook applies.
2. **Restore the general regime:** 25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket, 24-month claims period.
3. **Restore the separate Fundamental/Title regime** (100% cap, six years, outside basket and de minimis and knowledge bar). Delete the uniform-application wording.
4. **Add an express fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
5. **Replace the data-room and public-register disclosure** with specific fair disclosure. Delete 8.3 or replace it with a knowledge qualifier using named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Ask about the missing 1.3.
6. **Bluefen:** make effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions a pre-Completion condition. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable-endeavours-only.
7. **Riverlark:** require payout and direct repayment from Completion funds with effective security releases. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
8. **Bonuses:** add the AUD 420,000 DD-005 amount plus triggered on-costs as a specific line item in the funds flow, or require the Seller to fund them.
9. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity beyond SOW3, preserving the SOW3 cure. Do not assert the AUD 180,000 is owed.
10. **Incident:** require log preservation, investigation and regular updates. No breach, harm, notification or numeric demand is assumed in either direction.
11. **Sandbar:** assess each renewal's terms. Do not accept "ordinary course," and do not classify as Debt or deduct from price without assessment.
12. **Tax and IP:** keep open. Do not accept that they are settled under the general regime, and assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
13. **Title:** require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is not sufficient on its own.
14. **Mossvale and lease:** obtain the underlying provisions and confirm whether any consent or notice is required, rather than relying on the Seller's summary.

## Authority and limits

- The 20% cap, 18-month period and any post-Completion Riverlark release can only move with Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft. None is recorded, so none should be conceded.
- This review is based on the Seller's summary and disclosure letter. The underlying SPA clauses and data room documents should be checked directly before the mark-up goes out.
- NSW counsel should review enforceability, particularly the fraud carve-out and any limits on liability.
